guest.bio_context: Kelly Roach rose from poverty—growing up on the free lunch line—to becoming a senior vice president in a Fortune 500 company. She built her first business as a side hustle over five years while working full time, reaching one million dollars before transitioning to entrepreneurship full time. Within two years of full-time entrepreneurship, she scaled her core business to eight figures and has since built a portfolio of six companies, several of them multi-million dollar enterprises, with a goal to reach nine figures within ten years.

pending_qa.q: How does building multiple businesses at different growth stages improve coaching and mentorship quality?
pending_qa.r: Kelly explains that having companies at all different phases of the journey keeps her connected to what her startup-phase clients are experiencing, even while running a multi-eight-figure company. She also notes that maintaining businesses with different models, price points, and go-to-market strategies prevents her from teaching through only one singular approach, ensuring she can teach from a well-rounded perspective rather than defaulting to the one thing she knows.

pending_qa.q: How can time constraints from a full-time job accelerate efficiency and intentionality in building a side business?
pending_qa.r: Kelly reflects that having a full-time job while building her business forced her to develop discipline she still carries as a full-time entrepreneur. Because working 80 hours a week was off the table, she had to figure out how to be more efficient and intentional about what she was doing to get results in less time, which ultimately allowed her to put family first and invest in faith and other life priorities.

pending_qa.q: What are the key values and support systems women need to build both a thriving business and family life?
pending_qa.r: Kelly emphasizes knowing what your values are and being clear about them. She stresses that women must set themselves up at home with the right support system to make having both a business and family viable, and that many women claim they want both but fail to establish a strong team at home equivalent to their office team.
